subject: Commercial roadmap & evaluation milestones — Aurora Analytics
messages:
From: Simon Jennings <simon.jennings@aurora-analytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@aurora-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Commercial roadmap & evaluation milestones — Aurora Analytics

Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the performance looked promising for our private VPC use case. Elena and I chatted and we want to formalize a mutual action plan so procurement can see clear gates to move to an on-prem/VPC license. I've attached our initial MAP (Aurora_MAP_v1.xlsx) — high level asks:

- Pilot (6 weeks): validate latency targets on our internal data; target concurrency ~10 rps.
- PoC to Prod ramp (3 months): linear ramp to 200k tokens/day.
- Pricing: need committed discount tiers based on sustained monthly token commitments.
- Platform fee question: your platform fee model for Private (one-time vs annual) and any waiver for year 1.

Can you propose milestone-based commercial terms (pricing tiers, commits, and any ramp discounts) and a sample timeline we can show procurement? Also: Aurora requires an audit trail for data residency and SOC2 evidence as part of the contract.

Looking for a concise MAP and an SOW checklist we can move to legal.

Regards,
Simon Jennings
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurora Analytics

Attachment: Aurora_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 34KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simon Jennings <simon.jennings@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@aurora-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial roadmap & evaluation milestones — Aurora Analytics

Simon / Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks and the MAP draft. Attached is a Redwood MAP template (Redwood_MAP_template_v2.xlsx) with a milestone-driven commercial proposal. High level summary below so procurement can review quickly:

1) Pilot (6 weeks) — Proof of concept
   - Capacity: private VPC provisioned with 2x A100-equivalent nodes (dedicated)
   - SLAs: 95th pct token latency target of <120ms for 512-token requests
   - Cost: Pilot support billed at standard hosted rate (no platform fee credit applied)
   - Deliverables: latency report, KV/prefix caching config, SOC2 evidence bundle

2) Pilot->Prod Ramp (3 months) — Staged committed capacity
   - Commit Tiers (monthly sustained tokens):
     • Tier 1: 0–200k tokens/day — baseline per-token price $0.0009
     • Tier 2: 200k–1M tokens/day — per-token price $0.0007 (10% volume discount)
     • Tier 3: >1M tokens/day — per-token price $0.00055 (further discounts tied to 12-month commit)
   - Platform fee (Private/VPC): base annual platform fee of $75,000; options below for early-stage customers

3) Ramp incentives / discounts tied to MAP milestones
   - 30% discount on platform fee if Aurora signs a 12-month commit at Tier 2 or higher within 45 days after pilot completion
   - One-time onboarding credit equivalent to 1 month of committed spend for integration/testing
   - Option to convert unused pilot capacity as a credit against first monthly invoice

4) Licensing & compliance
   - Private deployment license (per-instance) + annual platform fee; SOW will call out KMS integration and audit log retention (90 days by default, extendable)
   - We will bundle SOC2 artifact package and a checklist for procurement (deliverable in week 1 of pilot)

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood and Aurora align on pilot success criteria (latency, throughput, integration checkpoints) — due EOD Wed 24 Feb
- If agreed, Redwood will issue an MOU with the milestone commercial terms above and a draft SOW for Aurora legal review within 3 business days of MOU sign
- We can offer an optional platform fee waiver of up to 50% for year 1 in exchange for a 12-month committed volume (we suggested 20–30% earlier; see Jon's note below for an alternative)

If Aurora prefers a staircase discount tied to monthly consumption rather than rigid tiers, we can model that as well — happy to put numbers next to the MAP items.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Neha — quick notes / negotiation levers from PM/finance side before we go to MOU:

- Platform fee structure: rather than a single large annual fee, offer a tiered platform fee tied to committed peak instances: e.g., $25k per provisioned instance annually (so a customer that needs 3 instances pays $75k). This maps better to Aurora's scaling profile.
- Intro incentive: offer a 50% platform fee discount for year 1 if they sign a 12-month commit at Tier 2+ within 45 days of pilot.
- Ramp protection: include an automatic 3-month price protection window post ramp in the MOU to prevent retroactive rate changes while they scale.
- Legal ask: include a list of SOC2 attachments we can provide and a statement of data residency controls for their legal team.

Also suggest we include a short list of redlines Redwood is unlikely to accept (data exfiltration, change of control indemnity) so procurement understands tradeoffs.

If you want, I can draft the MOU language for the platform fee concession and ramp protection.

Jonas Weber
Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com

Neha / Jonas —

Thanks for the detailed breakdown — that's exactly the kind of clarity procurement needs. A couple of quick points from our side before we lock the MOU:

- We prefer the per-instance platform fee model (Jon's approach) vs. a flat annual fee; please include expected instance sizing assumptions in the MOU.
- The 50% year-1 platform fee discount in exchange for a 12-month commit at Tier 2+ is acceptable, provided the SOW specifies the success criteria and an automatic credit if post-pilot latency targets aren't met.
- SOC2 evidence: we need an explicit list and estimated delivery dates (audit reports, control matrix, penetration test summary).

If you can send a short MOU with these bullet points plus a draft SOW and procurement checklist, I'll route to our legal and procurement. We aim to have a signed MOU within 10 business days of receiving your draft.

Regards,
Simon Jennings
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurora Analytics
